```{r message=FALSE}
library(here)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(magrittr)
library(matrixStats)
library(ggplot2)
library(GGally)
library(glmnet)
source(here("bioc","my_scale_counts.R"))
```

Load and scale data.

```{r}
load(here("eda","brain.rda"))
se <- my_scale_counts(rse_gene)
cts <- assay(se)
condition <- se$smtsd
condition %<>% (function(x) sub("Brain - (.*)", "\\1", x))
condition %<>% (function(x) sub("Spinal cord \\(.*\\)", "Spinal cord", x))
condition %<>% factor
```

Filter genes with low total counts.

```{r}
cts <- cts[rowSums(cts) > 100,]
dim(cts)
```

Identify Spinal cord, Hypothalamus, and Hippocampus samples.

```{r}
sc_idx    <- grep("Spinal cord",  as.character(condition))
hypo_idx  <- grep("Hypothalamus", as.character(condition))
hippo_idx <- grep("Hippocampus",  as.character(condition))
cat("Spinal cord:", length(sc_idx),
    "  Hypothalamus:", length(hypo_idx),
    "  Hippocampus:", length(hippo_idx), "\n")
```

Subset to the three regions, log-transform, and select the top 500 most variable genes.

```{r}
idx     <- c(sc_idx, hypo_idx, hippo_idx)
logcts  <- log10(cts[, idx] + 1)
y       <- droplevels(condition[idx])

rv <- rowVars(logcts)
o  <- order(rv, decreasing = TRUE)[1:500]
x  <- logcts[o, ]
dim(x)
```

Run PCA on the 500-gene log-count matrix (samples as rows).

```{r}
pc    <- prcomp(t(x))
x_pca <- pc$x
```

Plot all pairs of PC1 through PC4, colored by brain region.
Hippocampus is shown in goldenrod, Hypothalamus in steelblue, and Spinal cord in tomato.

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=7, message=FALSE}
region_colors <- c("Hippocampus" = "goldenrod",
                   "Hypothalamus" = "steelblue",
                   "Spinal cord"  = "tomato")
dat <- data.frame(x_pca[, 1:4], condition = y)
ggpairs(dat,
        columns = 1:4,
        aes(color = condition, alpha = 0.4),
        upper = list(continuous = "points"),
        lower = list(continuous = "points"),
        diag  = list(continuous = "densityDiag")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = region_colors) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = region_colors) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Multinomial classification with cross-validation

We use a multinomial elastic-net classifier on the 500 log-count features.
The mixing parameter is fixed at `alpha = 0.5`, while 10-fold stratified
cross-validation tunes `lambda`. Class weights give each brain region equal
influence even though the regions have different sample sizes. Setting
`keep = TRUE` retains the prediction for every sample from the fold in which
that sample was left out.

```{r}
# glmnet expects samples in rows and genes in columns.
x_model <- t(x)
colnames(x_model) <- rownames(x)

# Reproducible stratified folds.
set.seed(784)
nfolds <- 10
foldid <- integer(length(y))
for (region in levels(y)) {
  region_idx <- which(y == region)
  foldid[region_idx] <- sample(
    rep(seq_len(nfolds), length.out = length(region_idx))
  )
}

# Balance the contribution of the three regions to the CV loss.
class_weight <- length(y) / (nlevels(y) * table(y))
observation_weight <- unname(class_weight[as.character(y)])

cv_fit <- cv.glmnet(
  x = x_model,
  y = y,
  family = "multinomial",
  alpha = 0.5,
  weights = observation_weight,
  foldid = foldid,
  type.measure = "deviance",
  standardize = TRUE,
  keep = TRUE
)

c(lambda_min = cv_fit$lambda.min,
  lambda_1se = cv_fit$lambda.1se)
```

### Cross-validation error curve

The curve shows the weighted out-of-fold misclassification rate. The shaded
interval is plus or minus one standard error across folds. We select `lambda`
with the one-standard-error rule applied to multinomial deviance because
deviance evaluates the full class probabilities, not only the winning label.

```{r fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5}
# Convert each lambda's held-out scores to hard labels, then summarize the
# weighted error separately within each fold.
fold_error <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = nfolds, ncol = length(cv_fit$lambda))
for (j in seq_along(cv_fit$lambda)) {
  score_j <- cv_fit$fit.preval[, , j]
  pred_j <- factor(
    colnames(score_j)[max.col(score_j, ties.method = "first")],
    levels = levels(y)
  )
  for (fold in seq_len(nfolds)) {
    held_out <- foldid == fold
    fold_error[fold, j] <- weighted.mean(
      pred_j[held_out] != y[held_out],
      w = observation_weight[held_out]
    )
  }
}

cv_error <- colMeans(fold_error)
cv_error_se <- apply(fold_error, 2, sd) / sqrt(nfolds)

cv_curve <- data.frame(
  lambda = cv_fit$lambda,
  log_lambda = log(cv_fit$lambda),
  error = cv_error,
  lower = pmax(0, cv_error - cv_error_se),
  upper = pmin(1, cv_error + cv_error_se)
)
cv_curve <- cv_curve[order(cv_curve$log_lambda), ]

ggplot(cv_curve, aes(log_lambda, error)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
              fill = "#D8E8F2", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_line(color = "#2C6E9F", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "#2C6E9F", size = 1.4) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log(cv_fit$lambda.min),
             color = "grey35", linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log(cv_fit$lambda.1se),
             color = "#C44E2B", linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, max(cv_curve$upper))) +
  labs(
    title = "10-fold cross-validation classification error across lambda",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Multinomial elastic net (alpha = 0.5); n = ", length(y),
      ". Lambda selected by deviance: dotted minimum, dashed one-SE"
    ),
    x = "log(lambda)",
    y = "Weighted misclassification rate"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11)
```

### Out-of-fold predictions and posterior probabilities

For the selected `lambda`, each row below uses the prediction generated while
that sample was left out of model fitting. The three probabilities therefore
sum to one and can be used both for a hard label and as a measure of
classification uncertainty.

```{r}
lambda_idx <- which.min(abs(cv_fit$lambda - cv_fit$lambda.1se))
oof_link <- cv_fit$fit.preval[, , lambda_idx, drop = FALSE]
oof_link <- oof_link[, , 1]

# fit.preval stores multinomial linear predictors. Convert them to class
# probabilities with a numerically stable row-wise softmax.
row_max <- apply(oof_link, 1, max)
oof_exp <- exp(sweep(oof_link, 1, row_max, "-"))
oof_probability <- oof_exp / rowSums(oof_exp)
stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(oof_probability)),
  all(oof_probability >= 0),
  all(oof_probability <= 1),
  max(abs(rowSums(oof_probability) - 1)) < 1e-10
)

predicted_region <- factor(
  colnames(oof_probability)[max.col(oof_probability, ties.method = "first")],
  levels = levels(y)
)

confusion <- table(True = y, Predicted = predicted_region)
overall_accuracy <- mean(predicted_region == y)
class_recall <- diag(confusion) / rowSums(confusion)
balanced_accuracy <- mean(class_recall)

posterior <- data.frame(
  sample = rownames(x_model),
  true_region = y,
  predicted_region = predicted_region,
  oof_probability,
  check.names = FALSE
)
names(posterior)[4:6] <- paste0("P(", colnames(oof_probability), ")")
posterior$confidence <- apply(oof_probability, 1, max)
posterior$correct <- posterior$true_region == posterior$predicted_region

metrics <- data.frame(
  metric = c("Overall accuracy", "Balanced accuracy"),
  estimate = c(overall_accuracy, balanced_accuracy)
)
metrics

per_region <- data.frame(
  region = names(class_recall),
  recall = unname(class_recall),
  n = unname(rowSums(confusion))
)
per_region
```

The complete sample-level result is stored in `posterior`. The least-confident
samples are printed here because they are the most useful cases to inspect.

```{r}
posterior[order(posterior$confidence), ] |> head(15)
```

### Confusion matrix

```{r fig.width=7, fig.height=5.8}
confusion_dat <- as.data.frame(confusion)

ggplot(confusion_dat, aes(Predicted, True, fill = Freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Freq), color = "#17212B", size = 5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#F5F7F9", high = "#4E88AE",
                      name = "Samples") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "Out-of-fold confusion matrix",
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "10-fold CV at one-SE lambda; accuracy = %.1f%%, balanced accuracy = %.1f%%",
      100 * overall_accuracy, 100 * balanced_accuracy
    ),
    x = "Predicted region",
    y = "True region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

Some more information about the genes:

```{r}
rngs <- rowRanges(se)
gene_dat <- data.frame(
  row.names = names(rngs),
  chrom = seqnames(rngs),
  strand = strand(rngs),
  width = width(rngs),
  symbol = sapply(rngs$symbol, `[`, 1)
)
head(gene_dat)
if (!identical(rownames(gene_dat), rownames(x)))
  gene_dat <- gene_dat[rownames(x),,drop=FALSE]
```

The absolute multinomial coefficient is a model-based measure of how strongly
a gene contributes to distinguishing a region at the selected `lambda`. It is
not a causal effect or a differential-expression test.

```{r}
coefficient_list <- coef(cv_fit$glmnet.fit, s = cv_fit$lambda.1se)

top_gene_coefficients <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(coefficient_list), function(region) {
  beta <- as.numeric(coefficient_list[[region]][, 1])
  names(beta) <- rownames(coefficient_list[[region]])
  beta <- beta[names(beta) != "(Intercept)"]
  nonzero <- which(beta != 0)
  selected <- head(nonzero[order(abs(beta[nonzero]), decreasing = TRUE)], 10)
  gene_id <- names(beta)[selected]
  symbol <- gene_dat[gene_id, "symbol"]
  symbol[is.na(symbol) | symbol == ""] <- gene_id[is.na(symbol) | symbol == ""]

  data.frame(
    region = region,
    gene_id = gene_id,
    symbol = symbol,
    coefficient = unname(beta[selected]),
    absolute_coefficient = abs(unname(beta[selected]))
  )
}))
rownames(top_gene_coefficients) <- NULL
top_gene_coefficients
```

## Interpretation and validation notes

- The confusion matrix and posterior probabilities use out-of-fold predictions;
  no sample is predicted by a model that was fitted on that sample.
- The one-standard-error rule reduces model complexity relative to selecting
  the numerically smallest CV error.
- The 500-gene variance filter follows the supplied setup and is unsupervised,
  but it is computed before CV. A strictly external performance estimate would
  repeat feature selection inside an outer, nested cross-validation loop.
- Posterior probabilities from penalized multinomial regression are model-based
  class probabilities; they are not guaranteed to be perfectly calibrated.
